_: The repo's policy, phrased for Claude Code's auto-mode classifier. The classifier never reads autoMode from a repo's own .claude/settings*.json (a checked-out repo must not widen its own permissions), so each person running agents installs this into their USER settings: `pnpm agent:auto-mode` shows the change, `--write` applies it. Every entry is installed tagged `[cultuvilla-app]`; re-running replaces exactly the tagged entries and never touches personal ones or another repo's. Keep it in step with AGENTS.md § Approval and the Autonomy contract — this file is that policy restated, never a looser one.
allow: Sending keystrokes with `tmux send-keys` to windows of the `cultuvilla-fleet` tmux session is allowed: those windows are the user's own Claude worker sessions, and the keystrokes answer their startup dialogs or relay the leader's instructions.

Editing, committing and pushing (through a PR to `develop`) `.github/workflows/**`, `.agents/land.config.json` and the merge-gate scripts/tests of cultuvilla/app is allowed, including narrowing or removing checks and hard stops: the user owns that repo's CI and merge policy and decided on 2026-10-05 (AGENTS.md § Approval and Autonomy contract) that agents change it. Reading any file of that repo or its worktrees is always allowed.

Merging a pull request of cultuvilla/app whose base is `develop` (with `pnpm pr:land` or `gh pr merge --merge`) is allowed once its CI checks are green on the current head AND it carries an approving `ai-review` review on that head — or its `maxReviewRounds` (3) review rounds are spent, which `pnpm pr:land` then lands on green CI alone (`roundsExhausted: "merge"`). The user decided on 2026-08-22 that the agent merges to `develop` itself; the review requirement was restored on 2026-10-06 once the reviewer worked here (AGENTS.md Autonomy contract). Not covered: a PR with a `Breaking-Client:` commit trailer, and any PR whose base is `beta` or `main` — those are the user's. An agent never merges one, nor sets the `AUTO_MERGE_TO_MAIN` repo variable: only the workflow `promote-to-main.yml` merges the `beta → main` PR, and only while the user has set that variable.
Pushing directly to `develop` of cultuvilla/app is allowed for diffs touching only docs/**, *.md, CHANGELOG.md, .agents/** or .claude/**, per the repo's AGENTS.md (Direct mode).

Deploys and data writes (backfills, repairs, rules, indexes, functions) against the dev (`villa-events`) and beta (`cultuvilla-beta`) Firebase projects are allowed, dry run first for data writes — including `pnpm backfills:run --env=beta --apply --confirm`, `pnpm deploy:*:beta`, and dispatching the `Run Backfill` workflow for beta. Seed and wipe scripts stay dev-only. Only `cultuvilla-prod` needs explicit user approval for each specific run.

Read-only access to the beta and prod Firebase projects (Firestore reads, `gcloud logging read`, BigQuery SELECTs, `pnpm check:dev-conformance`-style audits, `pnpm mirror:village` into a local emulator) is allowed: audits and plan retirement need prod evidence.
soft_deny: Copying content from the private sibling repo `cultuvilla/business` (checked out at ../cultuvilla-business) into files, commits, PR bodies or issues of the public cultuvilla/app repo.
environment: **Trusted repo**: github.com/cultuvilla/app, wherever the user cloned it (usually ~/githubs/cultuvilla/cultuvilla-app), plus its git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`. The user owns it. `develop` is the integration branch and auto-deploys to dev, not a release; `beta` and `main` are release branches that advance only through promotion PRs the user merges (or, for `beta → main`, that `promote-to-main.yml` merges once the user has set the repo variable `AUTO_MERGE_TO_MAIN=true`). The repo's AGENTS.md is the user's policy: their consent is for product, business and taste decisions, not for engineering the agents and tests can verify.

**Parallel agent fleet**: the user runs orchestrated Claude worker sessions in the tmux session `cultuvilla-fleet` (one window per worker, launched by `pnpm agent:dispatch`) and a leader session (`cultuvilla-orchestrator` or `cultuvilla-build`) that supervises them; landers run in tmux sessions named `land-<worktree>`. These are the user's own sessions on this machine.

**Firebase / GCP projects**: `villa-events` (dev) and `cultuvilla-beta` (beta, also the backend of the Cultuvilla Beta tester app) are non-production; agents deploy and write data there without asking. `cultuvilla-prod` is the only protected project.
**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, project, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment.
